references.text: Jacob gave Joseph a special coat (kětōnet), the same coat that his brothers now dip in goat's blood to deceive their father.
Rebekah used goat skins to help Jacob deceive his father Isaac – now Jacob himself is deceived by his sons with goat's blood. Poetic justice.
The brothers send the bloody coat to Jacob and ask him to recognize it. Jacob concludes that Joseph has been torn apart by a wild animal.
Tamar asks Judah to 'recognize' (hakker-na) his pledge, using the same expression the brothers used toward Jacob about the coat – a thematic parallel of deception and recognition.
The brothers later acknowledge their guilt for what they did to Joseph, and Reuben reminds them that he warned them. Their conscience catches up with them.
Direct narrative connection: The verse describes the removal of the tunic which is then dipped in blood.
